name: Me-Sahab
title: The Royal Woman of Edom
summary: Me-Sahab was the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Me-Sahab (some translations interpret this differently). She is mentioned in the Bible as the mother of Hadar (or Hadad), one of the kings of Edom. She is one of the few women named in the Edomite king lists in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the List of Edomite Kings
keyEvents.description: Me-Sahab is mentioned as the daughter of Matred in connection with King Hadar's (Hadad's) lineage, the last king in the Edomite king list in Genesis.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Me-Sahab's name is repeated in 1 Chronicles in the enumeration of the kings of Edom, where she is again identified as the daughter of Matred.

keyEvents.title: The Kingdoms of Edom
keyEvents.description: Me-Sahab is linked to the royal lineage of Edom, which descends from Esau. The kings of Edom reigned before Israel had kings.

keyEvents.title: Descendants of Esau
keyEvents.description: The king list where Me-Sahab is mentioned is part of the broader account of Esau's descendants, who became the people of Edom.
